rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional sentence leaves its answer unstated according to Arabic linguistic principles; verse 14 supplies the suppressed consequence.
rows.anchor: The answer to the condition it states is suppressed in accordance with linguistic principles. Verse 14 ahead reveals this suppression.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The directives themselves express God’s grace: they guide people to repentance and reform, whereas their conduct would otherwise have earned wrath.
rows.anchor: The implication is that it is the consequence of God’s blessings and mercy and the fact that He accepts repentance

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The section recalls the hypocrites’ ifk campaign and exposes how a group of Muslims unwittingly joined it and rashly spread their propaganda.
rows.anchor: They inadvertently had become a part of this mischief and rather rashly started to spread the propaganda these hypocrites wanted to spread.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims should deal with one another in trust and give the benefit of the doubt; they must investigate fully before accepting or spreading a damaging report.
rows.anchor: the Muslims must base their mutual dealing on trust and give others the benefit of doubt.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage exposes hypocrites and their patrons trying to damage Muslims’ moral standing through rumors, and warns believers to guard against their efforts.
rows.anchor: the desire and effort of the hypocrites and their patronisers are exposed. Muslims must stand on guard against them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The directives also call for forgiving people who inadvertently became involved in the mischief.
rows.anchor: They are also told to forgive those who have inadvertently become a part of this mischief.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites’ slander at Banū Muṣṭaliq targeted ʿĀʾishah, the Mother of the Faithful.
rows.anchor: of Muṣ ṭ aliq to malign ‘ Ā’ishah (rta).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because this lie against a Mother of the Faithful is unworthy of mention, the Qur’an withholds its content and instead identifies its originators and spreaders, leaving a lesson for all.
rows.anchor: the Qur’ ān has not spoken about it any further.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims recognized the charge as slander and knew hypocrites were behind it, yet mass commotion led naïve people to repeat it without grasping the consequences.
rows.anchor: the naïve start to transmit it without realizing the implications.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “a group from among you” points to infiltrating hypocrites led by ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy; outwardly they resembled Muslims, enabling them to spread their poison and mislead simple people, so believers are warned.
rows.anchor: Their leader was ‘Abdull āh ibn Ubayy. Since in their outward behaviour they were not different from Muslims

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One good concealed in the trial was that Muslims could detect the dissident group hiding within their community and prevent its future disorder.
rows.anchor: The greatest good concealed in it was that Muslims were able to fully detect a dissident group that was hiding among them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second good was that the trial exposed concealed weaknesses among Muslims so they could be reformed in time.
rows.anchor: the weaknesses that were concealed among Muslims were fully highlighted as a result of this trial and were reformed at the right

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reforming these weaknesses through the trial was important for the community’s spiritual purification.
rows.anchor: The importance this has for the spiritual purification of the society is absolutely

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third good was that the event created suitable circumstances for directives to reform and organize society, making their significance clear.
rows.anchor: The third good found in it is that it created a very appropriate atmosphere for the revelation of many directives for the reformation and organization of the society.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word kibar means the real or greater part of a sin.
rows.anchor: means the real or greater part of a sin.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The one who took up its greater part” means the originator of the mischief: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy, whom Islahi calls a mean hypocrite and says was responsible for this and earlier disturbances.
rows.anchor: would mean “the person who is the originator of this mischief.” This reference is to ‘Abdullāh ibn Ubayy who was a very mean hypocrite.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites’ mischief will bring their doom: each person is punished in proportion to his part, while its actual instigator faces grave punishment in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: the person who is actually responsible for it will face a grave punishment in the hereafter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every Muslim deserves good opinion and the benefit of the doubt until shown otherwise; hearing a damaging claim is no basis for circulating it without solid proof.
rows.anchor: It is the right of every Muslim man and woman in an Islamic society that other people think well about them and give them the benefit of doubt.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ignoring an attack on another Muslim’s reputation is also wrong; defending each brother’s honor is an obligation.
rows.anchor: The proper attitude in this regard is to defend the honour of every brother because this is a person’s obligation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi contrasts this ethic with contemporary society, where people are presumed bad unless personal or collective interests favor them.
rows.anchor: Today the dominant view is that every person must be regarded as a bad person unless we have a vested interest in him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He criticizes rumor-spreading as a profession among journalists and writers, whose newspapers and magazines thrive on hearsay.
rows.anchor: There are so many journalists and writers in our society whose profession is to spend all their days and nights in trying to find and spread hearsay.
